transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Rec: automated
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Cloudline ML Eng), Ethan Morales (Platform Lead), Sara Li (Head of Data)

Summary (auto): walkthrough of mixed-precision strategy (INT8/FP8), tradeoffs between latency and quality, plan for pilot and concrete evals.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:07 Priya: hi, priya here. can hear you fine.
00:10 Ethan: ethan, yep.
00:12 Sara: sara on my side.
00:14 Liam: liam from redwood. we're excited to dig in.
00:18 Maya: cool, we're going to start with a short overview of mixed precision, then show the console Optimize suggestions, run through a few short audio-free examples - i mean text examples - and then dig into the fidelity vs latency numbers, and finish with next steps.

02:05 Maya: quick context so we don't re-cover: cloudline is trying to reduce token costs for real-time assist product, current stack is hosted API with batching at the edge, latency p95 is ~320ms, target is <200ms. also you flagged occasional hallucinations on safety-critical prompts.
02:29 Priya: correct, the p95 spikes are killing us during bursts, and int8 experiments we've run locally dropped quality unexpectedly on the legal-domain prompts.
02:40 Liam: yeah and that's typical — int8 often reduces headroom on rare-token distributions. fp8 tends to keep fidelity but is trickier to support on older GPUs.

05:02 Maya: first slide: "mixed precision options" - we recommend a progressive rollout: start with model-level FP8 where available, fallback to INT8 with per-prompt quality gating using the Optimize quality monitor.
05:35 Ethan: quick question — does redwood console expose per-route precision settings? i.e., can we route 20% of traffic through fp8 and keep 80% fp32?
05:45 Liam: yes, per-route and per-model variant. you can set traffic split in rollouts and define automatic rollback thresholds based on our evals. the console will show token-level cost delta as well.

07:30 Priya: during our local INT8 runs, we saw a 12% decrease in rouge on docs summarization but latency improved by 26%. curious what numbers you have for fp8.
07:44 Maya: good, we'll show a table — FP8 in our internal benchmarks often gives 10-15% latency improvement over fp32 with <2-3% quality delta on open-web prompts; INT8 gives larger cost wins but with wider variance.
08:10 Liam: important nuance: "quality" varies by evaluation metric and prompt distribution. Optimize suggests per-prompt qprofile which lets you pick per-prompt precision. so a high-sensitivity legal prompt can stay fp32 while casual chat goes int8.

10:15 Maya: demo time — opening the Console Optimize tab. (typing noises) apologies if the sample dataset loads slowly.
10:36 Maya: here's the recommended qprofiles panel; you can see candidate quantization profiles, estimated token-cost reductions, and a predicted fidelity score. note these are statistical estimates using our small eval harness.
10:50 Priya: where's the provenance of the fidelity estimate? is that from the eval set we uploaded?
10:55 Liam: currently it's a mix — if you upload a labeled eval set, the predictions are calibrated to that; otherwise we use a provider-agnostic proxy and warn about domain mismatch.

13:20 Maya: running a quick side-by-side: baseline fp32, fp8 candidate, int8 candidate on a short legal prompt set. I'll paste outputs into the chat.
13:45 Maya: (pastes link) https://redwood.example/bench/CLD-mix-20260207 — this points to a small sample and the gold reference.
14:05 Priya: getting that, thanks. loading... (pause) hmm i see the fp8 output retains clause structure better than int8 which seems to truncate or rephrase some clause connectors.
14:30 Sara: we can't tolerate those rewrites in compliance docs.
14:33 Liam: understood. this is where per-route gating helps. also worth noting we can tune the qprofile to preserve certain layers in higher precision to keep those clause tokens stable — it's not all-or-nothing.

17:12 Maya: here's a latency graph: p50/p95 for each profile on an A100-ish backend vs a 4090-class GPU. the delta is larger on consumer GPUs for int8 because kernel support differs.
17:30 Ethan: interesting, our infra uses mixed GPU fleet in the cloud provider, some older gen cards; how does redwood handle heterogeneous fleets?
17:44 Liam: smart routing — you can pin routes to hardware families or let the runtime auto-fallback to compatible variants. if a GPU doesn't support fp8 ops efficiently we route to a compatible fp32 or int8 fallback path, with cost/latency trade annotated.

20:02 Priya: about hallucinations — our legal prompts need exact quoting and non-invented clauses. is there a quality monitor that triggers on hallucination patterns?
20:14 Liam: yes, Optimize supports custom probes — you can define eval metrics like named-entity precision or citation fidelity; we run these continuously and emit alerts or hold rollouts if regressions exceed thresholds.

22:45 Maya: small demo of per-prompt qprofile: pick a label 'legal-clauses' and pin to "preserve-layer-precision: top 2 attention layers fp32", rest int8. applying now to 10% of traffic.
22:58 Priya: that granular control is great. will that require model reserialization?
23:05 Liam: sometimes yes — certain qprofiles require a slight reshard/quant artifacting step. we can do it online with zero-downtime if you have Dedicated capacity; otherwise there's a short model conversion window.

25:30 Ethan: cost question — can you give a back-of-envelope for token cost delta across the three modes: fp32, fp8, int8 on our current volume (estimated 300M tokens/month)?
25:45 Maya: at your volume rough numbers: fp32 baseline $X (placeholder), fp8 ~ 30-35% token-cost reduction, int8 ~ 55-60% but with quality caveats. we'll send exact numbers after we see your prompt mix.
26:12 Priya: please send the spreadsheet — the procurement folks will need it.

28:00 Maya: quick aside — we ran an internal rookies test where int8 created subtle paraphrase shifts in named entities; the Optimize quality monitor flagged them via strict string-match checks. that's why we advise staged rollouts.

30:22 Liam: switching to the "eval playback" feature: you can replay failed prompts across variants and see token-by-token diffs, attention heatmaps (approx), and KV-cache reuse stats. note transcription may say K-V cash sometimes in logs.
30:48 Priya: nice, the diff view will help our QA triage.

33:10 Maya: demo of auto-suggested profile: Optimize recommends an fp8-safe profile for 'assistant' route, suggests keeping embedding layers in fp16 while quantizing MLPs to int8 for cost-sensitive endpoints.
33:35 Sara: can we export those recommendations as terraform or a YAML config for our infra repo?
33:42 Liam: yes, Console has an "export config" -> YAML snippet and an API endpoint. we also emit a change log entry for audits.

36:00 Priya: one risk: we have on-prem pockets where GPUs do not support fp8 at all; will a mixed deployment (hosted + private infra) work with Redwood?
36:14 Maya: absolutely, Redwood Private supports hybrid routing — calls originating from private VPC can be routed to local on-prem endpoints for sensitive data, and traffic still flows through the same rollout config. we just annotate the model variant compatibility and cost delta.

38:50 Ethan: latency: you showed p95 numbers, but how do batching and prefix caching interact with quantization? our prefixes are often long for session state.
39:05 Liam: prefix/KV cache helps more with repeated context; quantization typically affects forward pass time per token. with large prefixes, the KV cache reuse reduces generated tokens so the net latency improvement from int8 can be smaller. Optimize simulates your prefix distribution if you upload request traces.

41:20 Priya: curious about the fidelity monitor thresholds: is there a typical guardrail value you use for legal workloads?
41:33 Maya: for high-sensitivity we recommend very strict thresholds — like <0.5% regression in entity recall and <0.2% in string-exact checks before full rollout. but we can tailor.

44:10 Liam: quick technical note — quantization noise sometimes concentrates in softmax tails; a mitigation is stochastic rounding and selectively preserving LN/LayerNorm in higher precision. our qprofiles let you configure these.
44:30 Priya: stochastic rounding — is that supported cross-hardware?
44:38 Liam: supported on newer kernels; on older hardware we emulate with small perf penalty. we'll flag compatibility.

47:05 Maya: live Q&A: Priya — any specific prompts you want us to run live now?
47:12 Priya: yes, one contract excerpt, short, 120 tokens. curious to see fidelity.
47:25 Maya: ok running: baseline fp32 output -- (paste) "Contract shall not be assigned without prior written consent..."
47:40 Maya: fp8 output -- (paste) "Contract shall not be assigned without prior consent from the party..."
47:55 Maya: int8 output -- (paste) "Contract may not be assigned unless consent is obtained."
48:05 Priya: int8 slightly rephrased and dropped 'written', that's unacceptable for us. fp8 looks okay but still softer wording.
48:20 Sara: that difference is a blocker for legal.
48:25 Maya: noted. recommendation: keep legal routes on fp32 or fp8 with stricter qprofile (preserve top layers). we can also add a downstream string-exact check gate that fails int8 responses and sends them to fp32 fallback.

50:30 Ethan: that fallback sounds operationally heavy — will that double egress costs when fallback happens?
50:45 Liam: fallback only triggers on flagged prompts; in practice with good gating and qprofile tuning fallback rate is <1-2%, so cost impact is limited. we can surface the projected fallback percentage in Console before rollout.

52:10 Maya: recap: pilot plan suggested — run a 2-week pilot, 10% traffic baseline, apply fp8 on low-sensitivity routes, int8 on experimental internal routes only. collect 1k prompts each from production-like traces, run eval harness and then a dedicated perf run.
52:40 Priya: sounds good. can you also include an action item to map which routes are 'sensitive'? we'll need a matrix.
52:50 Maya: yes we'll send a proposed sensitivity matrix template.

55:00 Liam: timeline — we can provision Dedicated trial capacity within 3 business days; full pilot setup with evals ~ 1 week after we receive prompt sets.
55:15 Priya: procurement needs pricing for Dedicated + Optimize features.
55:20 Maya: noted, we'll send pricing and sample contract language.

58:20 Sara: one last compliance item — audit logs must be retained 12 months and be searchable; does the Console support that retention?
58:33 Liam: yes, we have retention tiers; 12 months is available as part of enterprise package. logs are searchable and exportable for audits.

60:00 Maya: ok thanks everyone — finalizing next steps and we'll email the deck and notebooks. thanks for candid feedback.
60:10 Priya: thanks, useful session.
60:12 Ethan: great, appreciate it.
60:15 Sara: bye all.

Auto notes: references shared during call: demo bench link (https://redwood.example/bench/CLD-mix-20260207), Console quickstart, eval notebook (to be delivered), pricing spreadsheet (to be delivered).
